messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Elevated p95 latency and throughput drop observed on runtime-service after deploy 2026-03-17T02:10Z (v2.7.1) :rotating_light:
incidents-bot: affected route: /api/generate, region: us-west-2, symptom: sustained tail latency and microbatch queuing
maria: paging @oncall, looks like the new_batcher flag was flipped in the rollout earlier tonight
jake: saw it — traces show many requests falling back to the generic execution path, CPU queues stacking on GPU workers
sam: grabbing pager, taking initial lead. Can someone post quick perf numbers? :eyes:
ricardo: throwing numbers — 90m window since deploy:
```
- avg throughput: -22%
- p50: +10ms
- p95: +320ms
- error rate: +1.2ppt (mostly timeouts)
```
elena: customer-facing: support reported three customer timeouts in the last 30m, small-medium customers on reserved capacity affected
maria: deploy-bot shows rollout to 40% of fleet, can we throttle/stop?
deploy-bot: ROLLOUT PAUSED at 40% by automated threshold (latency spike)
jake: good — sounds like the batching heuristics in the feature flag are creating microbatch starvation, causing fallback to slower code paths
sam: quick mitigation options: (1) toggle new_batcher off (kill flag), (2) rollback to v2.7.0, (3) throttle traffic to older variant. Preferences?
ricardo: preference 1 then 2 if not stable. Kill-flag is fastest and non-disruptive to sessions
elena: I'll draft a short customer note if we toggle the flag, will need ETA and explanation
maria: @sam please execute kill-flag now, call it "new_batcher.off" and confirm
sam: running command now:
```
$ infra-ctl feature-toggle runtime-service new_batcher off --env prod --reason "latency regression v2.7.1"
Toggling feature new_batcher -> OFF
Propagation to control plane started
```
maria: seeing metrics tick — p95 trending down slowly
ricardo: p95 delta over 10m: 320ms -> 85ms, throughput back to -8% vs baseline, errors dropping
support-bot: opened ticket INC-2026-1137 to track customer reports, priority P2, notifying account teams
elena: posted short note to affected customers: "We're investigating a performance regression after a recent runtime deploy; temporary mitigation in progress. We'll update within 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:
jake: parallel ask: check if any nodes reverted to old kernel path, I want the node-level logs
sam: grabbing logs from a few examples — snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T02:15:42Z] worker=rt-23 exec_path=generic_fallback reason="batch_timeout" batch_size=1 queue_ms=210
[2026-03-17T02:15:42Z] worker=rt-45 exec_path=optimized_batch reason="ok" batch_size=8 queue_ms=12
```
maria: that matches microbatch starvation, small batches timeout and hit the fallback path which spikes latency for those traces
ricardo: impact estimate: ~3.6% of requests experienced p95 > 1s during the 40% rollout window, around 220k requests total affected, primarily interactive features with short prompts
elena: customer comms updated with estimated scope and mitigation steps; including option for account teams to request proactive support calls for high-value customers
sam: keeping rollout paused. if metrics remain stable for 10m we'll promote a patch build with a tweak to batching timeout heuristics
maria: action items: 1) confirm flag fully propagated (sam) 2) monitor metrics for 30m (ricardo) 3) open postmortem doc (maria) 4) coordinate rollback path if re-open (jake)
sam: flag fully propagated at ~02:18Z, control plane confirms 100% off for routes in prod
ricardo: metrics check at 02:25Z shows p95 stabilized near baseline, throughput recovering to -2% within 12 minutes
support-bot: customer ticket INC-2026-1137 updated: mitigation applied, monitoring for residual errors
elena: planning to send a follow-up at +45m with final impact and next steps
jake: note for root cause: need to audit batching heuristics + regression tests covering small prompt sizes; will add to backlog and label urgent
maria: oncall handoff: @sam keep monitoring for next 2 hours, i'll take the 06:00 handoff and prepare the postmortem
sam: acknowledged, will escalate if we see any reversion or new error spikes
incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: latency regression mitigated via feature toggle at 02:18Z; monitoring continues.
thread_summary: Feature-flagged microbatcher rollout caused microbatch starvation and fallback to slower execution path after a partial deployment. Team paused rollout and toggled feature off; p95 and throughput recovered. Customer-facing comms and a follow-up postmortem were initiated.
